name: phase2_index_lifecycle_and_immutability
description: A compiled pact binary rebuilds a disposable index over a signed fork, merge, and checkpoint without changing canonical or trust bytes.
given: signed fork and merge commits with reversed advisory timestamps
when: the operator rebuilds, logs, queries, shows, and verifies
the live SQLite file is removed and rebuilt
then: causal batches follow dependencies rather than observed_at
logical digest and normalized results are identical
objects, trust, checkpoint, and heads are unchanged
index output omits payload, evidence, and private key material

name: phase2_filters_pagination_and_partial_replica
description: Fixed queries cover all ten filter families, causal and supersession links, restart-safe pages, and explicit local incompleteness.
given: real signed events in exact, descendant, and boundary namespaces
when: the compiled binary rebuilds and queries through fresh processes
the operator paginates across ordered and unresolved rows
cursors are reused after restart, same-source rebuild, query change, and source change
then: OR within a family and AND across families are exact
supersedes does not add causal order
coverage is partial while the index remains current
malformed, mismatched, and stale cursors fail safely
strict verify and checkpoint refuse incomplete history

name: phase2_unusable_index_recovery
description: Each unusable regular-database state refuses indexed reads and recovers only through explicit rebuild from canonical bytes.
given: independent real repositories with stale, corrupt, incompatible, or self-consistent row-divergent regular SQLite files in a safe index directory
then: status names the exact state
indexed reads fail with a safe typed code
show and strict canonical verification stay available where required
recovered results match canonical events

name: phase2_reachable_cli_limits
description: Reachable query limits pass at the approved boundary and fail at the first excess without echoing hostile input.
given: oversized and secret-like cursor or filter input
when: the compiled query runs with 64 and 65 family values, 256 and 257 total values, and limits 1000 and 1001
then: exact boundaries pass
first excess returns resource_limit or usage
diagnostics omit raw cursor and secret-like input

name: phase2_hostile_canonical_and_index_paths
description: Malformed canonical trees, non-regular object entries, symlink traps, and oversized sparse SQLite files fail closed before unsafe traversal or open.
given: fresh real stores with hostile filesystem entries
a real FIFO named as a canonical object
a sparse live SQLite file of 2147483649 bytes
when: the compiled binary rebuilds or inspects status
bounded canonical lookup targets the FIFO
then: malformed, non-regular, and symlinked paths are refused before read
the oversized index is corrupt without being opened
canonical and trust bytes do not change

name: phase2_real_process_concurrency_and_interruption
description: Real query, rebuild, and commit processes serialize to contract-valid states, and termination before rename preserves the prior live index.
given: additional signed history large enough to observe an exact .build-*.sqlite3 file
when: query, rebuild, and commit processes race
a rebuild process is killed after its exact temp file appears and before publication
then: responses are complete current results or typed stale refusals
the prior live bytes remain unchanged and never corrupt or partial-build
status ignores the temp file
explicit rebuild recovers to current and strict verify passes

name: phase2_full_resource_profile_lower_layer_map
description: Full-profile hostile graph, canonical scan, object, event, edge, cursor, result, and SQLite limits stay at streaming or algorithm layers rather than giant duplicate E2E fixtures, while a reachable signed local-reference cycle runs through the compiled CLI.
given: a real signed commit whose two events form a local caused_by cycle
when: exact-bound and first-excess unit or real-file integration tests run
strict verify and index rebuild inspect the signed cycle
then: 4096/4097 depth and frontier bounds hold
100000 objects, 1 GiB canonical bytes, 250000 events, one million edges, 4 MiB objects, 16 MiB results, 4096-byte cursors, and 2 GiB SQLite are pinned and bounded
the compiled CLI rejects the cycle as a canonical hard failure without publishing an index or mutating protected bytes

name: setup_compiled_guided_lifecycle
description: A compiled pact binary configures and resumes real local setup state, while real PTY prompts require one approved plan before mutation.
when: fully flagged setup processes create, resume, conflict, and race
a guided terminal setup is declined and accepted
then: repo, key, trust, verification, and index actions converge in fixed order
reruns preserve exact bytes
decline writes nothing
one plan and one confirmation precede accepted mutation
private key fields stay outside repositories and output
